--- title: "JupyterLab" jupyter: php --- Once `juphyter install` has written a kernelspec, JupyterLab lists it in the launcher under the name `--display-name` gave it, or the name the install command chose by itself. A new notebook with that kernel runs PHP cells. ```bash vendor/bin/juphyter install --name php85 --display-name "PHP 8.5" jupyter lab ``` The kernel has to be installed where the running JupyterLab looks. `juphyter install` writes to `JUPYTER_DATA_DIR` when it is set, and otherwise to the per-user data directory, which is `~/Library/Jupyter` on macOS and `~/.local/share/jupyter` on Linux. `jupyter kernelspec list` shows what a JupyterLab will find. ## What a notebook shows A cell's result appears under it as an `Out[n]`. State carries from one cell to the next, the stop button interrupts a running cell, and restarting the kernel starts a new PHP session with nothing bound. Tab completion covers three things: the session's variables after a `$`, the declared functions and classes for a bare prefix, and a value's public members after `->` or `::`. The continuation prompt works as well, so an unterminated block or string leaves the cell open rather than running it. ## Plots JupyterLab draws a phiz plot from the Vega-Lite specification. juphyter publishes the specification under `application/vnd.vegalite.v5+json`, which is the newest Vega-Lite MIME type JupyterLab's bundled renderer defines, and the specification itself is Vega-Lite 6. Publishing a version 6 specification under the version 5 MIME type was the one display risk worth checking before relying on it, because the renderer could reject a construct it does not know. It does not: JupyterLab's bundled Vega-Lite 5.6.1 compiled sixteen phiz-generated specifications without complaint. No mime-renderer extension is needed, and phiz needs no change. The static SVG that juphyter also publishes is not JupyterLab's path. It is there for Quarto's PDF and docx output and for any front end without JavaScript, and it is the fallback if a later Vega-Lite construct does turn out to be rejected. The HTML representation is not JupyterLab's path either. JupyterLab does not execute scripts in `text/html` output, and phiz's `embed()` output is a container plus a script tag, so it would render as an empty box. Quarto's HTML output is what that representation is for. ## Tables A phibble data frame renders as an HTML table. The table's own style block uses JupyterLab's CSS variables for its fonts and colors, with plain fallbacks, so it follows the light and dark themes rather than fighting them. ::: {#e4aee235 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.php .cell-code} DataFrame::fromRows([ ['front end' => 'JupyterLab', 'plot from' => 'the Vega-Lite spec', 'table from' => 'text/html'], ['front end' => 'Quarto HTML', 'plot from' => 'the HTML embed', 'table from' => 'text/html'], ['front end' => 'Quarto PDF', 'plot from' => 'the static SVG', 'table from' => 'the parsed table'], ]); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
A tibble: 3 × 3
front end <chr>plot from <chr>table from <chr>
1JupyterLabthe Vega-Lite spectext/html
2Quarto HTMLthe HTML embedtext/html
3Quarto PDFthe static SVGthe parsed table
``` ::: ::: ## Notebooks and projects Jupyter starts a kernel with the notebook's own directory as its working directory, and the engine walks up from there looking for `vendor/autoload.php`. A notebook saved inside a Composer project therefore has that project's classes in scope, including its phibble and phiz, with nothing to configure. A notebook kept outside the project it works on needs the autoloader named. `JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD` names one for a launch, `juphyter install --autoload` names one for a kernelspec, and an `autoload` entry in a `juphyter.json` beside the notebook names one for a project. A `juphyter.json` can also set the memory limit and add to the include path: ```json { "autoload": "../app/vendor/autoload.php", "memory_limit": "512M", "include_path": "lib" } ``` ## Converting a notebook `quarto convert` turns a `.ipynb` into a `.qmd` and back, and `nbconvert` exports a notebook to HTML or PDF from Python. Both work on a PHP notebook without knowing anything about PHP, because what they read is the notebook format rather than the language. [Quarto](quarto.qmd) covers rendering a document directly.
